headline: High-risk write-capable Goose paired with read-only LlamaFactory creates default prompt-injection, data-flow, and cascading-error exposure; compliance risk is low.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can read/write the filesystem and use MCP, so it can ingest artifacts that LlamaFactory or its workflows place in shared files. LlamaFactory itself has no shared-channel surface, so the interaction is one-way and not a guaranteed bridge. The pathway exists in default Goose configurations, but the pair lacks a documented direct channel, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF Goose reads instructions from files that LlamaFactory can write or influence in the same workspace, prompt injection is possible.
IF the two agents are connected through a shared filesystem or MCP-backed artifact flow, attacker-controlled content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable MCP access for Goose on shared projects.
Require manual review of any file Goose consumes from LlamaFactory.
Use read-only mounts for LlamaFactory outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches source code and files in cwd and has broad network egress, while LlamaFactory is read-only and networkless. If Goose is pointed at sensitive files that LlamaFactory also processes or summarizes, data can leave the local environment through Goose’s outbound calls. LlamaFactory alone does not leak, but the pair creates a default workspace-to-egress path.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in Goose's workspace, Goose can transmit their contents to configured model providers.
IF LlamaFactory outputs are copied into Goose inputs, those contents can be exfiltrated via Goose network egress.
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of the shared workspace.
Run Goose with a restricted egress policy.
Use separate service accounts and credentials.
Redact files before Goose reads them.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on outbound model calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose can write the filesystem and modify git state, but LlamaFactory has no write, git, or network capabilities. There is no overlapping mutable resource in the profiles, so direct capability conflict is limited. The only plausible conflict is indirect via shared files, which is narrower than the rubric’s medium/high cases.
conditions: IF both agents are given write access to the same directory, Goose can overwrite artifacts produced by the other workflow.
IF Goose is connected to a shared git checkout, concurrent commits can conflict.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Lock the git working tree during Goose runs.
Make LlamaFactory outputs immutable.
Run Goose on a copy of the repository.
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can generate and modify code or files that LlamaFactory may later consume, but LlamaFactory has no verification or critical-evaluation surface in the profile. That makes A-to-B propagation plausible through shared files, even though B is not an action-taking agent. The absence of a documented verification step pushes this above low.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory consumes Goose-produced files without independent validation, Goose errors can cascade into downstream outputs.
IF Goose commits incorrect artifacts and LlamaFactory later trains or reports on them, the error propagates.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Validate Goose outputs before LlamaFactory consumes them.
Use schema checks on shared files.
Keep generated artifacts separate from source inputs.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Goose handles model-provider keys and extension tokens and can access user files, while LlamaFactory is unverified but appears local-only with no network or file access. The pair does not show a residency or certification mismatch in the profiles, so compliance risk is limited to local handling hygiene rather than a clear breach pathway. The other agent is not cited because no compliance surface is exposed there.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in Goose's workspace, local handling and logging controls must be enforced.
IF extension tokens are stored alongside sensitive files, accidental disclosure becomes possible.
mitigations: Store secrets in a dedicated vault.
Exclude regulated data from Goose workspaces.
Review local logs before sharing.
Rotate any exposed extension tokens.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
